question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Diminish
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Weaken.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Diminish" is a verb which means to make or become less, smaller or weaker; to reduce in size, strength, importance or intensity. (कम होना / घटाना / कमज़ोर करना)

◦ Its closest synonym among the options is "weaken", which also means to make less strong or less powerful.

◦ Example: Regular exercise diminishes/weakens the risk of heart disease, and long illness diminished his strength.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Demote" means to lower someone in rank or position (पदावनत करना) — it applies to a person's post, not to a general reduction. Its antonym is "promote".

• Option 2 "Relegate" means to push down to a lower/inferior position or category (निम्न स्थान पर भेजना), e.g., a football club is relegated to a lower division. It is not a general synonym of "diminish".

• Option 3 "Prevent" means to stop something from happening (रोकना) — stopping is not the same as reducing gradually.

NOTE

• Synonyms of diminish: decrease, lessen, weaken, dwindle, wane, abate, subside, curtail, shrink.

• Antonyms of diminish: increase, enlarge, augment, amplify, expand, magnify.

• Frequently asked SSC pair: "diminishing returns" (ह्रासमान प्रतिफल) — an economics term meaning progressively smaller gains from each extra unit of input.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who loves or collects books
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Bibliophile.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Bibliophile" is a person who loves, reads or collects books. (पुस्तक-प्रेमी)

◦ Word formation: Greek biblio- = "book" + -phile = "one who loves". So biblio + phile = book-lover.

◦ Example: A true bibliophile, she owned first editions of every novel she admired.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Anglophile" = a person who admires England, the English people or English culture (Anglo = English).

• Option 2 "Heliophile" = a person (or plant) that loves or thrives in sunlight (helio = sun).

• Option 3 "Paedophile" = a person who is abnormally/criminally attracted to children (paedo = child) — a negative term that does not fit here.

NOTE

• Other "-phile" words often asked in SSC exams: Bibliophile (books), Cinephile (films), Francophile (France), Audiophile (high-quality sound), Oenophile (wine), Xenophile (foreigners).

• Related words: Bibliography (a list of books consulted), Bibliomania (an obsessive craze for collecting books), Bibliotheca (a library or book collection).

• The opposite is Bibliophobe (one who hates or fears books).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) We are living / (B) here since / (C) the summer / (D) of last year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part (A) "We are living" contains the error. When an action began at a point in the past and is still continuing, and the sentence uses "since", the correct tense is the present perfect continuous — "has/have been + V-ing" — not the present continuous.

◦ Incorrect: We are living here since the summer of last year.

◦ Correct: We have been living here since the summer of last year.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Part (B) "here since" is correct — "since" is properly used with a point of time (the summer of last year).

• Part (C) "the summer" and Part (D) "of last year" are grammatically correct noun phrases indicating that point of time.

NOTE

• Rule: With "since / for" expressing duration up to the present, use the Present Perfect or Present Perfect Continuous, never the Present Continuous or Simple Present.

◦ "I have been waiting for two hours." (NOT "I am waiting for two hours.")

◦ "She has known him since 2015."

• since + point of time (since Monday, since 5 o'clock, since 2019, since last summer).

• for + period of time (for two hours, for three years, for a long time).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Suresh has been learning Tamil ________ two months.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. for.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by "two months", which is a period/length of time, not a point of time. With a period of time in the present perfect continuous we use the preposition "for".

◦ Correct: Suresh has been learning Tamil for two months.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "from" indicates a starting point and is normally paired with "to/till" (from Monday to Friday); it is not used with the present perfect to show duration.

• Option 2 "since" is used only with a point of time — "since June", "since Monday", "since two months ago". "Since two months" alone is wrong.

• Option 3 "before" means earlier than a given time and does not express continuing duration.

NOTE

• Golden rule: for + length of time (for two months, for five years, for a while); since + point of time (since 2020, since morning, since he left).

• Both are used with the Present Perfect / Present Perfect Continuous tense: "He has worked here for ten years" / "He has worked here since 2014".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

Rina’s house is at a stone’s throw from the school.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A very short distance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a stone's throw (away)" means a very short distance; very near/close by — literally, as far as one could throw a stone. (बहुत कम दूरी पर / पत्थर फेंकने की दूरी पर)

◦ Correct sense: Rina's house is very close to the school.

◦ Example: The hotel is just a stone's throw from the railway station.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "A very long distance" is the exact opposite of the idiom's meaning.

• Option 2 "Next to" means immediately adjoining/adjacent, which is stronger and more literal than the idiom — a stone's throw means nearby, not necessarily touching.

• Option 4 "Not very close to" again reverses the sense.

NOTE

• Other idioms meaning "very near": "within spitting distance", "a hop, skip and a jump away", "round the corner", "at hand".

• Idioms meaning "very far": "at the back of beyond", "the ends of the earth", "a far cry from".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Accompanyment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Accompanyment" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "accompaniment" — meaning something that goes along with or supplements another thing, or the musical support played behind a singer. (संगत / साथ में दी जाने वाली वस्तु)

◦ Spelling key: AC + COM + PA + NI + MENT. When the suffix "-ment" is added to "accompany", the final -y changes to -i: accompany → accompaniment.

◦ Example: Rice is the usual accompaniment to this curry. / She sang to the accompaniment of a piano.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Wrestler" (a person who wrestles — पहलवान) is correctly spelt: W-R-E-S-T-L-E-R (silent "w").

• "Debatable" (open to argument or dispute — बहस योग्य) is correctly spelt; the final "e" of "debate" is dropped before "-able".

• "Discrepancy" (a difference or inconsistency between two things — विसंगति/अंतर) is correctly spelt: DIS + CREP + AN + CY.

NOTE

• Rule: A word ending in a consonant + y changes y → i before most suffixes: accompany → accompaniment, happy → happiness, marry → marriage, beauty → beautiful.

• Exception: keep the "y" before "-ing" — accompanying, marrying, studying.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Mohan unknowingly altered salt instead of sugar to the dessert making it taste terrible.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. added salt instead of sugar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb must fit the structure "___ something TO the dessert". Only "add" collocates with "to" in this sense — "added salt to the dessert". "Add" means to put one thing together with another. (मिलाना / डालना)

◦ Correct: Mohan unknowingly added salt instead of sugar to the dessert, making it taste terrible.

◦ The context (the dessert "tastes terrible") confirms that salt was put into the dish by mistake.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Altered" means changed or modified (बदलना). One does not "alter salt to a dessert" — the phrase is grammatically and semantically wrong.

• Option 2 "Anguished" means caused severe mental pain / to be in agony (पीड़ा देना) — it cannot take "salt" as an object.

• Option 3 "Amplified" means made larger, louder or stronger (बढ़ाना, विशेषकर ध्वनि) — used for sound or effect, not for putting an ingredient into food.

• Option 4 "Abridged" means shortened/condensed (संक्षिप्त करना), used of books, speeches, texts.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: add something to something; mix something with something; sprinkle something on/over something; pour something into something.

• Distinguish: adopt (to take up/accept), adapt (to adjust), adept (skilled), add (to put in) — a very common SSC confusion set.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

The actor decided to live life in the fast lane.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A life filled with excitement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "(life) in the fast lane" means an exciting, eventful and often risky or extravagant lifestyle, full of activity, glamour and pleasure. (रोमांच और उत्तेजना से भरा जीवन)

◦ Correct sense: The actor decided to live an exciting, glamorous and eventful life.

◦ Example: After winning the lottery he began living life in the fast lane — parties, travel and fast cars.

• The expression comes from the "fast lane" of a motorway, used by the quickest vehicles; figuratively it stands for a hectic, high-pressure, thrill-filled way of living.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Dropping charges of crime" has nothing to do with the idiom — it is a legal expression.

• Option 3 "Racing away to the moon" is a literal, invented phrase, not the idiomatic meaning.

• Option 4 "A life of extreme speed" is the literal reading of "fast lane". Idioms must be interpreted figuratively, so this is a distractor — the idiom refers to excitement and glamour, not to physical speed.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "live it up" (enjoy oneself lavishly), "paint the town red" (celebrate wildly), "burn the candle at both ends" (exhaust oneself with too much activity).

• Its opposite is "life in the slow lane" — a quiet, relaxed, unhurried way of living.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Sanjana rubbed her eyes hardly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. hardly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hardly" does not mean "in a hard manner"; it is an adverb of degree meaning "scarcely / almost not at all". The sentence intends to say that she rubbed her eyes with force, so the correct adverb is "hard".

◦ Incorrect: Sanjana rubbed her eyes hardly. (= she almost did not rub them)

◦ Correct: Sanjana rubbed her eyes hard.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Sanjana" (subject), "rubbed" (correct past tense of "rub") and "her eyes" (object) are all correct.

• Words like hardly, scarcely, barely, rarely, seldom are negative adverbs — they already carry a negative sense, so no extra "not" is used with them: "He can hardly speak" (NOT "He cannot hardly speak").

NOTE

• Similar adjective/adverb pairs where the "-ly" form changes meaning completely:

◦ hard (with effort) vs hardly (scarcely) — "He works hard" / "He hardly works".

◦ late (not early) vs lately (recently).

◦ near (close) vs nearly (almost).

◦ most (the greatest amount) vs mostly (mainly).

• Structure point: "hardly ... when", "scarcely ... when" and "no sooner ... than" are followed by inversion — "Hardly had she left when it began to rain".

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

I asked my friend to ___________________ against her employers who are doing wrong to her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. fight fire with fire.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "fight fire with fire" means to respond to an attack by using the very same methods/tactics that one's opponent is using. (जैसे को तैसा जवाब देना / ईंट का जवाब पत्थर से देना)

◦ The context — employers who "are doing wrong to her" — shows that the friend is being treated unfairly and is being advised to hit back with the same weapons.

◦ Correct: I asked my friend to fight fire with fire against her employers who are doing wrong to her.

◦ Example: When his rivals spread rumours about him, he decided to fight fire with fire.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Fine words butter no parsnips" is a proverb meaning mere talk/flattery achieves nothing; action is needed. It is a complete saying and cannot be slotted after "to".

• Option 2 "Finders keepers, losers weepers" is a children's saying meaning whoever finds something is entitled to keep it. It is irrelevant here and is also a full sentence.

• Option 3 "Fight the good fight" means to strive persistently for a worthy moral cause; it is normally used absolutely (not with "against" a person) and lacks the "retaliate in kind" sense demanded by the context.

NOTE

• Related idioms of retaliation: "give someone a taste of their own medicine", "an eye for an eye", "tit for tat", "pay someone back in their own coin".

• Note the fixed form: "fight fire with fire" — the preposition never changes.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains a misspelt word.

The single most important factor that distinguishes those of us who succed in any venture and those of us who don’t is this ‘instant coffee’ attitude.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. succed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Succed" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "succeed", a verb meaning to achieve the aim or result one wanted; to prosper. (सफल होना)

◦ Spelling key: SUC + CEED — double "c" and double "e" (-ceed, not -ced).

◦ Correct: ... those of us who succeed in any venture ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Distinguishes" (from distinguish — to recognise or show the difference between things; अंतर करना) is correctly spelt.

• "Venture" (a risky or daring undertaking, an enterprise; उद्यम/जोखिम भरा कार्य) is correctly spelt.

• "Attitude" (a settled way of thinking or feeling; दृष्टिकोण) is correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Only three English verbs end in "-ceed": succeed, proceed, exceed. One ends in "-sede": supersede. All the rest end in "-cede": precede, recede, concede, secede, intercede, accede.

• Word family of succeed: success (noun), successful (adjective), successfully (adverb), succession, successor, successive.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

A night alone / in a hotel / can be lonely prospect.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. can be lonely prospect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Prospect" is a singular countable noun, so it must be preceded by a determiner (article). The indefinite article "a" is missing before "lonely prospect".

◦ Incorrect: ... can be lonely prospect.

◦ Correct: ... can be a lonely prospect. ("a" is used because "lonely" begins with the consonant sound /l/.)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "A night alone" is correct — the article "a" is properly used with the singular countable noun "night".

• "in a hotel" is correct — "in" is the right preposition of place and "a" is the correct article.

• "No error" cannot be chosen because a definite error (the missing article) exists.

NOTE

• Article rule: Every singular countable noun needs a determiner — a/an, the, this/that, my/his, one, etc. "He is doctor" ✗ → "He is a doctor" ✓.

• Use a before a consonant sound (a university, a one-rupee coin) and an before a vowel sound (an hour, an MBA, an honest man).

• "Prospect" here means the possibility or expectation of something happening (संभावना).

question:
Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

The new restaurant on Main Street is cheap than the old one.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. is cheaper than.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" is a signal of the comparative degree. "Cheap" is a short adjective, so its comparative is formed by adding -er → "cheaper".

◦ Incorrect: The new restaurant on Main Street is cheap than the old one.

◦ Correct: The new restaurant on Main Street is cheaper than the old one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "the older one" is wrong — the sentence compares the new restaurant with the already existing ("the old one"); changing it to "the older one" does not remove the actual grammatical error, which lies in "is cheap than".

• Option 2 "in Main Street" is unnecessary — the standard American/neutral usage for a named street with an address on it is "on Main Street"; the original is acceptable.

• Option 3 "newer restaurant" is wrong — no comparison of newness is being made, and "the new restaurant" is already correct.

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: cheap – cheaper – cheapest; big – bigger – biggest; happy – happier – happiest.

• One-syllable and some two-syllable adjectives take -er/-est; longer adjectives take more/most (more expensive, most expensive).

• Never use a double comparative ("more cheaper") or a comparative without "than" when a comparison is intended.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

My relatives shall have reached Amritsar by now.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. shall.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence expresses a strong assumption/logical certainty about a completed action — "by now they have surely arrived". For such a presumption, the correct modal is "must" (or "will/should"), not "shall".

◦ Incorrect: My relatives shall have reached Amritsar by now.

◦ Correct: My relatives must have reached Amritsar by now.

• "Shall" with the third person ("my relatives") expresses command, promise, threat or determination, which is clearly not the intended meaning here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "My" is a correct possessive adjective before the noun "relatives".

• "Reached" is the correct past participle used after "have"; note that "reach" is used without a preposition before a place — "reached Amritsar" (NOT "reached at Amritsar").

• "By now" is a correct adverbial phrase used with perfect forms to mean "before this moment".

NOTE

• Modals of deduction (present/past):

◦ must have + V3 = certain that it happened ("He must have left").

◦ may/might have + V3 = possible that it happened.

◦ can't have + V3 = certain that it did not happen.

• Traditional rule: shall with I/We for simple future; will with He/She/They/You. Reversing them adds the sense of determination, promise or command.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Group of bees
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Swarm.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "swarm" is the correct collective noun for bees (and for other flying insects such as flies, locusts and gnats). (मधुमक्खियों का झुंड)

◦ Correct: A swarm of bees attacked the intruders.

◦ "Swarm" also works as a verb: "Bees swarmed around the hive."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Gaggle" is the collective noun for geese (on the ground); geese in flight form a "skein".

• Option 2 "Shoal" is used for fish (also "school of fish").

• Option 4 "Pack" is used for wolves, dogs or hounds (also a pack of cards).

NOTE

• Common collective nouns asked in SSC exams: a swarm of bees, a flock of sheep/birds, a herd of cattle, a pride of lions, a troop of monkeys, a school/shoal of fish, a litter of puppies, a pack of wolves, a fleet of ships, a bunch of keys/grapes, a galaxy of stars, a bevy of girls, a catalogue of books.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Crude
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Refined.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Crude" means raw, unprocessed, unpolished; or rude, vulgar and lacking sophistication. (कच्चा / असंस्कृत / अशिष्ट)

◦ Its antonym is "refined", meaning purified/processed or cultured, polished and elegant in manner. (परिष्कृत)

◦ Example: Crude oil is processed in a refinery to give refined petroleum products. / His crude jokes shocked the refined audience.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Primitive" (belonging to an early, undeveloped stage — आदिम) is a synonym, not an antonym, of crude.

• Option 1 "Patient" (able to endure delay calmly — धैर्यवान) and Option 4 "Observant" (quick to notice things — प्रेक्षणशील) are unrelated to the meaning of crude.

NOTE

• Synonyms of crude: raw, unrefined, coarse, rough, vulgar, rudimentary, primitive.

• Antonyms of crude: refined, polished, cultured, sophisticated, processed, elegant.

• Static link: Crude oil is the unprocessed petroleum extracted from the earth; India's largest crude refinery is at Jamnagar, Gujarat.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Can you quote any _______ in your favour?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. precedent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "precedent" is an earlier event, decision or case that is regarded as an example or rule to be followed in similar situations later (especially in law). (पूर्व-उदाहरण / नज़ीर)

◦ The verb "quote" collocates naturally with "precedent" — one quotes/cites a precedent to support one's own position, which matches "in your favour".

◦ Correct: Can you quote any precedent in your favour?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "answer" does not fit — one gives an answer, one does not "quote an answer in one's favour".

• Option 2 "summary" (a short account of the main points) is not something quoted to support an argument.

• Option 3 "lines" is too vague; "quote a few lines" is possible, but "any lines in your favour" is unidiomatic and does not convey supporting authority.

NOTE

• Word family: precedent (noun — an earlier example), precede (verb — to come before), preceding (adjective — coming before), unprecedented (adjective — never done or known before).

• Legal usage: courts "set a precedent", "follow a precedent" or "overrule a precedent". In India, under Article 141, the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts — the doctrine of precedent (stare decisis).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Assasin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Assasin" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "assassin" — a person who murders an important or famous person, usually for political or religious reasons. (हत्यारा — विशेषकर किसी प्रमुख व्यक्ति का)

◦ Spelling key: AS + SAS + SIN — there are two pairs of "s" (a-s-s-a-s-s-i-n), and the word ends in "-sin".

◦ Example: The assassin was arrested within hours of the killing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Insurance" (an arrangement giving financial protection against loss — बीमा) is correctly spelt.

• "Mischievous" (naughty; causing trouble — शरारती) is correctly spelt; note there is no "i" after the "v" — it is mischiev-ous, NOT "mischievious".

• "Inexpressible" (too great or intense to be described in words — अवर्णनीय) is correctly spelt with the suffix "-ible".

NOTE

• Word family: assassin (noun — the killer), assassinate (verb), assassination (noun — the act).

• The word comes from Arabic hashshashin, a medieval sect said to have carried out political murders.

• Other frequently misspelt SSC words: accommodation, occurrence, embarrassment, questionnaire, millennium, harass, committee.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Buying a new car can cost an arm and a leg.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Be expensive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "cost an arm and a leg" means to be extremely expensive; to cost a very large amount of money. (बहुत महँगा होना)

◦ Correct sense: Buying a new car can be very expensive.

◦ Example: That designer handbag cost her an arm and a leg.

• The image behind the idiom is that the price is so high that one would have to give up one's limbs to pay it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Be free" (costing nothing) is the exact opposite.

• Option 2 "Be affordable" (within one's means) and Option 3 "Be reasonable" (not too costly) both contradict the idiom.

NOTE

• Other idioms about high cost: "cost a fortune", "cost a pretty penny", "pay through the nose", "break the bank", "daylight robbery".

• Idioms about low cost: "dirt cheap", "a steal", "for a song", "cost next to nothing".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Insist
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Persist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Insist" means to demand or state something firmly and refuse to give way; to keep pressing for something. (आग्रह करना / ज़ोर देना)

◦ Its closest synonym here is "persist", which means to continue firmly in an opinion or course of action in spite of opposition. (डटे रहना / लगे रहना)

◦ Example: She insisted on paying the bill and persisted until we agreed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Resist" means to oppose or withstand (विरोध करना) — it is close to the opposite of insisting on something.

• Option 3 "Heist" means a robbery or burglary (डकैती) — a noun, completely unrelated.

• Option 4 "Assist" means to help (सहायता करना) — unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of insist: persist, urge, press, demand, maintain, assert, emphasise, stress.

• Prepositions: "insist on/upon something" (She insisted on going) and "insist that + clause" (He insisted that she come).

• Word family: insistent (adjective), insistence (noun); persistent (adjective), persistence (noun).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

There are several reasons why people might 1)_________ that homework is an unnecessary burden on children. Firstly, there is evidence to support the idea that homework 2)_________nothing to improve educational outcomes. Countries such as Finland, where school children are not given homework, regularly top international educational league tables and outperform nations where setting homework is the norm. Secondly, many parents would agree that the school day is already 3)_________, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home. 4)_________, it is recognised that play time is just as 5)_________as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. argue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the modal verb "might" ("people might ______ that homework is ..."). Every modal auxiliary (can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must) is followed by the bare infinitive (V1) — the base form of the verb without "to" and without any -s/-ed/-ing ending.

◦ Correct: There are several reasons why people might argue that homework is an unnecessary burden on children.

• "Argue" here means to put forward reasons in support of a view; to contend. (तर्क देना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "be argues" is doubly wrong — a finite "-s" form cannot follow "be", and "be" cannot follow "might" with a main verb attached this way.

• Option 2 "have argue" is wrong — after "have" the past participle (V3) is required ("have argued"), not the base form.

• Option 3 "argues" is wrong — the "-s" form is used only with a third-person singular subject in the simple present, and never after a modal.

NOTE

• Rule: Modal + V1 (bare infinitive). "She can swim", "You must go", "He might come".

• Contrast the perfect modal: modal + have + V3 — "He might have argued".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

There are several reasons why people might 1)_________ that homework is an unnecessary burden on children. Firstly, there is evidence to support the idea that homework 2)_________nothing to improve educational outcomes. Countries such as Finland, where school children are not given homework, regularly top international educational league tables and outperform nations where setting homework is the norm. Secondly, many parents would agree that the school day is already 3)_________, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home. 4)_________, it is recognised that play time is just as 5)_________as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. does.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the blank is "homework", an uncountable (singular) noun. By the rule of subject–verb agreement, a singular subject in the simple present takes the "-s" form of the verb — hence "does".

◦ Correct: ... evidence to support the idea that homework does nothing to improve educational outcomes.

• The expression "do nothing to + verb" means to have no effect at all in bringing something about.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "do" is the plural form and would need a plural subject ("homeworks" is not used in English; homework is always uncountable).

• Option 1 "will does" is wrong — after the modal "will" only the bare infinitive can follow ("will do").

• Option 2 "has do" is wrong — after "has" the past participle is required ("has done").

NOTE

• Uncountable nouns that are commonly mistaken for plurals and always take a singular verb: homework, information, furniture, advice, luggage, machinery, news, equipment, scenery, poetry, stationery.

◦ "The news is encouraging." / "This information is correct." / "Homework does not always help."

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

There are several reasons why people might 1)_________ that homework is an unnecessary burden on children. Firstly, there is evidence to support the idea that homework 2)_________nothing to improve educational outcomes. Countries such as Finland, where school children are not given homework, regularly top international educational league tables and outperform nations where setting homework is the norm. Secondly, many parents would agree that the school day is already 3)_________, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home. 4)_________, it is recognised that play time is just as 5)_________as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. long enough.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence complains that the school day already takes up so much time that children come home "too tired to do further study". The adjective that describes the duration of a day is "long", and the adverb "enough" is correctly placed after the adjective.

◦ Correct: ... the school day is already long enough, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home.

• The clue words "already" and "too tired" confirm the sense of sufficient (indeed excessive) length.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "big enough" is wrong — "big" refers to size, not to the length of time of a school day.

• Option 3 "not enough" reverses the meaning; it would suggest the school day is too short, contradicting "too tired to do further study".

• Option 4 "enough of" needs a following noun ("enough of the work") and cannot stand alone here.

NOTE

• Placement rule for "enough":

◦ After adjectives/adverbs — "old enough", "fast enough", "long enough".

◦ Before nouns — "enough money", "enough time".

• Contrast with "too": "too + adjective (+ to-infinitive)" shows excess in a negative sense — "too tired to study".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

There are several reasons why people might 1)_________ that homework is an unnecessary burden on children. Firstly, there is evidence to support the idea that homework 2)_________nothing to improve educational outcomes. Countries such as Finland, where school children are not given homework, regularly top international educational league tables and outperform nations where setting homework is the norm. Secondly, many parents would agree that the school day is already 3)_________, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home. 4)_________, it is recognised that play time is just as 5)_________as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Finally.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage lists reasons in a clear sequence of discourse markers: "Firstly, there is evidence ... Secondly, many parents would agree ... ______, it is recognised that play time is ...". The blank introduces the last item in the list, so the linker required is "Finally". (अंत में / आख़िरकार)

◦ Correct: Finally, it is recognised that play time is just as beneficial as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Similarly" shows likeness between two ideas, but this sentence introduces a new and final reason, not a parallel one.

• Option 2 "Normally" and Option 4 "Usually" are adverbs of frequency/habit; they do not signal the closing item of an enumeration.

NOTE

• Sequencing linkers: Firstly / First of all → Secondly → Thirdly → Then / Next → Finally / Lastly / In conclusion.

• Other linker families useful for SSC cloze tests: contrast (however, nevertheless, on the contrary), addition (moreover, besides, furthermore), cause–effect (therefore, hence, consequently), example (for instance, namely).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

There are several reasons why people might 1)_________ that homework is an unnecessary burden on children. Firstly, there is evidence to support the idea that homework 2)_________nothing to improve educational outcomes. Countries such as Finland, where school children are not given homework, regularly top international educational league tables and outperform nations where setting homework is the norm. Secondly, many parents would agree that the school day is already 3)_________, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home. 4)_________, it is recognised that play time is just as 5)_________as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. beneficial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "as + adjective + as" is used to show equality. The sentence compares play time with study time "from the perspective of brain development", so the adjective must be a positive one — "beneficial", meaning favourable, advantageous, producing good results. (लाभदायक)

◦ Correct: ... it is recognised that play time is just as beneficial as study time from the perspective of brain development.

• The whole paragraph argues in favour of less homework and more play, so a word of praise is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "soon" is an adverb of time and cannot describe play time in this comparison of value.

• Option 3 "bad" reverses the writer's argument — the passage is defending play time, not criticising it.

• Option 4 "confidential" (meant to be kept secret — गोपनीय) is completely out of context.

NOTE

• Comparison of equality: as + adjective/adverb + as → "as beneficial as", "as tall as", "as quickly as". The negative form may use "not so ... as".

• Word family: benefit (noun/verb), beneficial (adjective — advantageous), beneficiary (noun — one who receives a benefit), benefactor (noun — one who gives help).

question: What does the term ‘interest’ refer to in banking?
option_1: The additional amount earned on a loan or deposit
option_2: The amount of money deposited into a bank account
option_3: The value of a currency in relation to other currencies
option_4: The fee charged for withdrawing money from an ATM
solution_text:
The correct answer is The additional amount earned on a loan or deposit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In banking, "interest" is the additional amount paid or earned over and above the principal — the price of borrowing money or the reward for saving it. (ब्याज)

◦ On a deposit, the bank pays interest to the customer.

◦ On a loan, the customer pays interest to the bank.

• It is normally expressed as a percentage per annum (rate of interest) of the principal amount.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 describes a deposit, Option 3 describes the exchange rate, and Option 4 describes an ATM/service charge — none of these is interest.

• Types of interest: simple interest (calculated only on the principal) and compound interest (calculated on principal plus accumulated interest).

NOTE

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) influences interest rates in the economy through the repo rate (rate at which RBI lends to banks) and the reverse repo rate (rate at which RBI borrows from banks).

• Banks quote lending rates on the basis of the MCLR and the External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR) systems.

question: Bihu is a folk dance of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bihu" is the most famous folk dance of Assam, performed during the Bihu festival, especially Rongali/Bohag Bihu which marks the Assamese New Year and the arrival of spring in mid-April. (बिहू — असम)

• It is performed by young men and women in colourful traditional dress to the beat of the dhol, pepa (buffalo-horn pipe), gogona and taal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Assam celebrates three Bihus: Rongali/Bohag Bihu (April — spring/sowing), Kongali/Kati Bihu (October — austerity), and Bhogali/Magh Bihu (January — harvest feast).

• Other dances of Assam: Bagurumba (Bodo tribe), Jhumur, and the classical Sattriya (introduced by Srimanta Sankardeva).

NOTE

• Folk dances of some other states: Bihar — Jat-Jatin, Bidesia, Jhijhiya; Chhattisgarh — Panthi, Raut Nacha, Karma; Arunachal Pradesh — Bardo Chham, Ponung; Punjab — Bhangra, Giddha; Gujarat — Garba, Dandiya.

question: In which year did Lord Curzon announce the partition of Bengal during the British rule in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1905.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, announced the Partition of Bengal in 1905; it came into effect on 16 October 1905. (बंगाल का विभाजन — 1905)

• The official reason given was administrative convenience, as Bengal was too large a province, but the real motive was to divide Hindus and Muslims and weaken the growing nationalist movement — the classic policy of "divide and rule".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The partition created two provinces: Eastern Bengal and Assam (capital Dacca) and the rest of Bengal (capital Calcutta).

• It triggered the Swadeshi and Boycott Movement (1905), in which foreign goods were burnt and Indian goods promoted. Rabindranath Tagore composed "Amar Sonar Bangla" and Raksha Bandhan was observed as a symbol of unity.

• The partition was annulled in 1911 by Lord Hardinge II, at the Delhi Durbar, when the capital of India was also shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.

NOTE

• Lord Curzon (1899–1905) is also associated with the Indian Universities Act 1904, the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act 1904 (creation of the Archaeological Survey of India in its modern form) and the Police Commission (1902).

question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the Power Sector’s Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme?

1) The Prime Minister launched the Ministry of Power’s flagship Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme in 2022.

2) This scheme is aimed at improving the operational efficiencies and financial sustainability of distribution companies.

3) From FY 2022-23 to FY 2027-28, the scheme aims to provide financial assistance to DISCOMs.

4)This scheme proposes to provide 25 crore Smart Prepaid meters to consumers all over the country.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 4.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) is the flagship scheme of the Ministry of Power. (पुनर्गठित वितरण क्षेत्र योजना)

◦ Statement 1 is correct — the Prime Minister formally launched the scheme in July 2022 during the "Ujjwal Bharat Ujjwal Bhavishya – Power @2047" programme.

◦ Statement 2 is correct — its declared objective is to improve the operational efficiency and financial sustainability of DISCOMs (distribution companies) by reducing AT&C losses and the ACS–ARR gap.

◦ Statement 4 is correct — it proposes the installation of about 25 crore smart prepaid meters for consumers across the country.

◦ Statement 3 is INCORRECT — the scheme provides assistance from FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26, not from FY 2022-23 to FY 2027-28.

• Hence the correct combination is 1, 2 and 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• RDSS was approved by the Cabinet in July 2021 with an outlay of about ₹3.03 lakh crore, including a Central government share of roughly ₹97,631 crore.

• Targets: reduce AT&C (Aggregate Technical and Commercial) losses to 12–15% and bring the ACS–ARR gap to zero by 2024-25.

NOTE

• Earlier power distribution schemes merged/subsumed into RDSS: IPDS (Integrated Power Development Scheme) and DDUGJY (Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana).

• Other power-sector schemes: UDAY (financial turnaround of DISCOMs, 2015), SAUBHAGYA (household electrification, 2017).

question: ‘Mein Kampf’ is the autobiography of which world personality?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Adolf Hitler.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mein Kampf" (German for "My Struggle") is the autobiography-cum-political manifesto of Adolf Hitler, the dictator of Nazi Germany. (मेरा संघर्ष — एडोल्फ हिटलर)

• Hitler dictated it while imprisoned in Landsberg Prison after the failed Beer Hall Putsch of 1923; the first volume was published in 1925 and the second in 1926.

• The book sets out his ideas of anti-Semitism, racial superiority of the "Aryan" race, Lebensraum (living space) and extreme nationalism.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Adolf Hitler became Chancellor of Germany in 1933, founded the Third Reich, and his invasion of Poland in 1939 started the Second World War. He died in April 1945.

• Robert Mugabe was the long-serving President of Zimbabwe; Albert Einstein was the physicist who gave the theory of relativity and won the Nobel Prize (1921) for the photoelectric effect; Charlie Chaplin's autobiography is titled "My Autobiography" (he also satirised Hitler in the film "The Great Dictator").

NOTE

• Famous autobiographies: My Experiments with Truth (Mahatma Gandhi), The Story of My Life (Helen Keller), Wings of Fire (A. P. J. Abdul Kalam), Long Walk to Freedom (Nelson Mandela), An Autobiography (Jawaharlal Nehru).

question: What is the geographic location of the world's largest coral reef, known as the Great Barrier Reef?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Australia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Great Barrier Reef", the world's largest coral reef system, lies in the Coral Sea off the coast of Queensland, north-eastern Australia. (ग्रेट बैरियर रीफ — ऑस्ट्रेलिया)

• It stretches for over 2,300 km, covers about 3.44 lakh sq km, and is made up of nearly 2,900 individual reefs and 900 islands. It is the largest structure on Earth built by living organisms and is visible from space.

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1981.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Corals are built by tiny marine animals called polyps, which secrete calcium carbonate. They live in symbiosis with algae called zooxanthellae.

• Corals need warm (20–30°C), shallow, clear, salty water with plenty of sunlight — hence reefs occur mainly between 30°N and 30°S.

• Coral bleaching occurs when rising sea temperatures force the polyps to expel their algae, turning the coral white; the Great Barrier Reef has suffered repeated mass bleaching events.

NOTE

• Switzerland is a landlocked country in Europe, so it can have no coral reef; China and Ireland have no reef of this scale.

• In India, coral reefs are found in the Gulf of Mannar, Gulf of Kachchh, Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep.

question: To which Gharana did Gangubai Hangal primarily belong?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kirana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gangubai Hangal (1913–2009) was a legendary Hindustani classical vocalist who belonged to the Kirana Gharana. (किराना घराना — गंगूबाई हंगल)

• She was famous for her deep, powerful contralto voice and for her rendering of khayal. She learnt under Sawai Gandharva (Rambhau Kundgolkar), a leading disciple of Ustad Abdul Karim Khan, the founder of the Kirana Gharana.

• She was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1971) and the Padma Vibhushan (2002), besides the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Kirana Gharana takes its name from Kairana in Uttar Pradesh. It emphasises the slow, elaborate development of the raga (vilambit khayal) and precise intonation of swaras.

• Other great Kirana Gharana singers: Ustad Abdul Karim Khan, Sawai Gandharva, Bhimsen Joshi, Prabha Atre and Hirabai Barodekar.

NOTE

• Major Hindustani vocal gharanas: Gwalior (the oldest), Agra, Kirana, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala, Rampur-Sahaswan and Bhendibazaar.

• Patiala Gharana — Bade Ghulam Ali Khan; Agra Gharana — Faiyaz Khan; Banaras Gharana — associated with thumri and tabla (Girija Devi, Kishan Maharaj).

question: Popular since ancient eras for the trading of livestock, ___________, which is a month-long event, takes place on the auspicious occasion of Kartik Purnima in the month of November near Harihar Nath temple.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sonepur Mela.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Sonepur Mela" (also called Harihar Kshetra Mela) is held at Sonepur in Saran district, Bihar, at the confluence of the Ganga and Gandak rivers, near the famous Harihar Nath temple. (सोनपुर मेला — बिहार)

• It begins on Kartik Purnima (November) and runs for about a month, and is celebrated as Asia's largest cattle/livestock fair, where elephants, horses, camels, cattle and birds are traded.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Harihar Nath temple is believed to have been built by Lord Rama, and later renovated by Raja Man Singh of Amber. The name "Harihar" combines Hari (Vishnu) and Har (Shiva).

• Historically, even Chandragupta Maurya is said to have bought elephants and horses at this fair.

NOTE

• Option 3 "Pushkar Mela" is the famous camel fair of Pushkar, Rajasthan, also held on Kartik Purnima, but it is not near the Harihar Nath temple.

• Option 2 "Rajgir Mela/Malmas Mela" is held at Rajgir, Bihar; Option 4 "Ardh Kumbh" is held every six years at Prayagraj/Haridwar.

question: How many states were selected in Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (GKRA) 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6 states.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (GKRA)" was launched on 20 June 2020 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi from Telihar village, Khagaria district, Bihar, to provide immediate employment and livelihood to migrant workers who returned to their villages during the COVID-19 lockdown. (गरीब कल्याण रोजगार अभियान — 6 राज्य)

• It covered 116 districts across 6 states — Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jharkhand and Odisha — each district having received more than 25,000 returnee migrants.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It was a 125-day mission-mode campaign with a resource envelope of about ₹50,000 crore.

• The Abhiyaan involved the convergence of 25 works/schemes across 12 different ministries, such as rural roads (PMGSY), Jal Jeevan Mission, Anganwadi centres, community sanitary complexes, railway works, and Bharat Net.

• The Ministry of Rural Development was the nodal ministry for coordination.

NOTE

• Other COVID-19 relief measures of 2020: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Yojana (PMGKY), Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY — free foodgrains) and the Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan economic package.

question: The celebrated folk artist Gulabo Sapera, recipient of Padma Shri Award in 2016, is an exponent of ___________ dance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalbeliya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gulabo Sapera is the world-renowned exponent of the "Kalbeliya" dance of Rajasthan, and was awarded the Padma Shri in 2016. (कालबेलिया नृत्य — गुलाबो सपेरा)

• The Kalbeliya dance is performed by women of the nomadic Kalbeliya (snake-charmer) community. The dancers wear long, black swirling skirts (angrakhi and lehenga) and move in serpentine, swaying motions imitating a snake, to the music of the been (pungi), khanjari and dholak.

• UNESCO inscribed Kalbeliya folk songs and dances of Rajasthan on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Tippani" is a folk dance of Gujarat, performed by women labourers who beat the floor with long sticks (tippani).

• Option 3 "Bhavai" is both a folk theatre form of Gujarat and a Rajasthani dance in which the performer balances pots on her head while dancing on a sword or glass.

• Option 4 "Dandiya" (Dandiya Raas) is the stick dance of Gujarat, performed during Navratri.

NOTE

• Other folk dances of Rajasthan: Ghoomar (the state's best-known dance), Kachhi Ghodi, Chari, Terah Taali, Gair and Kathputli (puppetry).

question: Which Indian musician was awarded the Grammy award for his Album ‘Planet Drum’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zakir Hussain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Zakir Hussain, the legendary tabla maestro, was part of the album "Planet Drum", which won the Grammy Award for Best World Music Album in 1992 — the first ever Grammy given in that category. (ज़ाकिर हुसैन — प्लैनेट ड्रम)

• "Planet Drum" was a percussion collaboration created with Mickey Hart (drummer of the Grateful Dead) and other world percussionists.

• The follow-up album "Global Drum Project" (with Mickey Hart) won another Grammy in 2009.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Zakir Hussain is the son of the great tabla player Ustad Alla Rakha. He has been honoured with the Padma Shri (1988), Padma Bhushan (2002) and Padma Vibhushan (2023).

• He was also a founding member of the fusion group "Shakti" with guitarist John McLaughlin.

NOTE

• Other Indians associated with the Grammy Awards: Pandit Ravi Shankar (multiple Grammys), A. R. Rahman (two Grammys in 2010 for Slumdog Millionaire), Ricky Kej, Falguni Shah (Falu) and Sivamani/Selvaganesh (with the group Shakti in 2024).

• Sivamani is a famous percussionist, Trilok Gurtu a jazz-fusion percussionist and Darshan Doshi a contemporary Indian drummer.

question: Which of the following is NOT a part of the six communication mail channels in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Monthly channel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India Post organises the movement of mail through six dedicated mail channels/streams: the Rajdhani Channel, Metro Channel, Green Channel, Business Channel, Bulk Mail Channel and Periodical Channel. (भारतीय डाक के छह मेल चैनल)

• There is no "Monthly channel", so that is the odd one out.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Rajdhani Channel — quick and reliable transmission of mail between the national capital and state capitals.

• Metro Channel — mail service among the six metro cities (Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad).

• Green Channel — for local mail within a city.

• Business Channel — for business/bulk customers' mail.

• Bulk Mail Channel — for customers posting mail in bulk.

• Periodical Channel — for newspapers, magazines and registered periodicals.

NOTE

• India Post, under the Department of Posts (Ministry of Communications), runs the largest postal network in the world, with over 1.5 lakh post offices.

• The PIN (Postal Index Number) code system was introduced in 1972 by Shriram Bhikaji Velankar; India has 9 PIN zones.

question: Which of the following is an example of a non-debt capital receipt in the government budget?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sale of government-owned land.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Capital receipts are government receipts that either create a liability or reduce the government's assets. They are of two kinds:

◦ Debt-creating capital receipts — borrowings, market loans, external loans, treasury bills.

◦ Non-debt capital receipts — those that do not create any liability, i.e., recovery of loans, disinvestment (sale of shares of PSUs) and the sale of government assets/land.

• Hence the "Sale of government-owned land" is a non-debt capital receipt — it reduces an asset but creates no obligation to repay. (गैर-ऋण पूंजीगत प्राप्तियाँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Loans from international financial institutions" is a debt-creating capital receipt (it must be repaid).

• Option 3 "Interest payment on government bonds" is an expenditure (revenue expenditure) of the government, not a receipt.

• Option 4 "Tax revenue" is a revenue receipt, not a capital receipt.

NOTE

• Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure − Total Receipts excluding borrowings (i.e., revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts).

• Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts. Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit − Interest Payments.

• The Union Budget is presented under Article 112 of the Constitution as the "Annual Financial Statement".

question: Visva Bharati a famous educational institute was founded in 1921 by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Visva-Bharati at Santiniketan, Birbhum district, West Bengal, was founded by Rabindranath Tagore in 1921. (विश्व-भारती — रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर, 1921)

• Tagore had started a school there in 1901 (Brahmacharya Ashrama); in 1921 it was expanded into a university based on the ideal of learning in harmony with nature, expressed in its motto "Yatra Visvam Bhavatyekanidam" — "Where the whole world meets in a single nest".

• It was declared a Central University and an Institution of National Importance by an Act of Parliament in 1951.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) was the first Asian to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1913) for "Gitanjali". He wrote India's national anthem "Jana Gana Mana" and Bangladesh's "Amar Sonar Bangla", and renounced his knighthood after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919).

• The Prime Minister of India is the Chancellor (Paridarshak/Visitor) of Visva-Bharati.

NOTE

• Vinoba Bhave led the Bhoodan Movement (1951); Mother Teresa founded the Missionaries of Charity (1950) in Calcutta; Swami Chinmayananda founded the Chinmaya Mission (1953).

question: How many women boxers from India won gold medals in the Women's World Boxing Championship 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At the IBA Women's World Boxing Championships 2023, held in New Delhi (India), four Indian women boxers won gold medals — India's best-ever performance at the event. (चार स्वर्ण पदक)

◦ Nitu Ghanghas — 48 kg (minimumweight)

◦ Nikhat Zareen — 50 kg (flyweight)

◦ Lovlina Borgohain — 75 kg (middleweight)

◦ Saweety Boora — 81 kg (light heavyweight)

• India finished at the top of the medal tally with these four golds.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India had earlier won four golds only once before — in 2006 at New Delhi, when Mary Kom was among the champions.

• Nikhat Zareen thus became a two-time world champion (2022 Istanbul and 2023 New Delhi).

• Lovlina Borgohain won a bronze medal at the Tokyo Olympics 2020.

NOTE

• M. C. Mary Kom is a six-time World Champion (2002, 2005, 2006, 2008, 2010, 2018) and an Olympic bronze medallist (London 2012).

• The world governing body for boxing at that time was the International Boxing Association (IBA); boxing at the Olympics is now overseen by World Boxing.

question: Famous Bollywood actress Hema Malini is a trained ______ dancer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The veteran Bollywood actress Hema Malini, popularly called the "Dream Girl", is a trained Bharatanatyam dancer. (भरतनाट्यम — हेमा मालिनी)

• She has performed and choreographed several dance ballets such as Meera, Durga, Radha–Krishna and Draupadi, and runs the Natya Vihar Kalakendra dance school.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni. It was earlier known as Sadir/Dasiattam and was revived in the 20th century by Rukmini Devi Arundale (founder of Kalakshetra) and E. Krishna Iyer.

• Hema Malini received the Padma Shri (2000) and has been a Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha and later Lok Sabha from Mathura).

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Whose prior recommendation is required to introduce money bills in state legislature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Governor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A Money Bill can be introduced in the State Legislative Assembly only with the prior recommendation of the Governor, and only in the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha), never in the Legislative Council. (राज्यपाल की पूर्व सिफारिश)

• This is provided by Article 207 of the Constitution; Article 199 defines what a Money Bill is at the state level.

• The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly certifies whether a bill is a Money Bill, and his decision is final.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• At the Centre, the corresponding provisions are Article 110 (definition of a Money Bill) and Article 117 (prior recommendation of the President for introduction in the Lok Sabha).

• A Money Bill deals with taxation, borrowing, the Consolidated Fund/Contingency Fund, appropriation of money, etc.

• The Legislative Council can only delay a Money Bill for 14 days and can suggest changes which the Assembly may accept or reject.

NOTE

• The Advocate General of a State (Article 165) is the highest law officer of the state, appointed by the Governor; the Attorney General (Article 76) is the corresponding officer at the Centre.

question: RK Narayan is the author of _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Guide.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Guide" (1958) is a celebrated novel by R. K. Narayan (Rasipuram Krishnaswami Iyer Narayanaswami), one of the greatest Indian writers in English. (द गाइड — आर. के. नारायण)

• It won him the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1960 and was made into the famous Hindi film "Guide" (1965) starring Dev Anand and Waheeda Rehman.

• Most of his stories are set in the fictional South Indian town of "Malgudi".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other works of R. K. Narayan: Swami and Friends, The Bachelor of Arts, The English Teacher, The Financial Expert, The Man-Eater of Malgudi, Malgudi Days and The Vendor of Sweets.

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1964) and the Padma Vibhushan (2000).

NOTE

• Option 2 "Far From the Madding Crowd" is by Thomas Hardy; Option 3 "Godan" is by Munshi Premchand; Option 4 "Untouchable" is by Mulk Raj Anand.

• R. K. Narayan, Mulk Raj Anand and Raja Rao are considered the trinity of early Indian English fiction.

question: Where is the Qutub Minar situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Qutub Minar" is situated in the Mehrauli area of Delhi. (कुतुब मीनार — दिल्ली)

• It is the tallest brick minaret in the world, about 72.5 metres (approx. 73 m) high with 379 steps and five storeys.

• Its construction was begun in 1199 by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the founder of the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty, and completed by his successor and son-in-law Iltutmish; the upper storeys were later repaired by Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Qutub Complex also contains the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque (the earliest surviving mosque in India), the Iron Pillar of Chandragupta II (famous for being rust-free for over 1,600 years), Alai Darwaza (built by Alauddin Khalji, 1311) and the unfinished Alai Minar.

• The minar is built of red sandstone and marble and carries inscriptions from the Quran in Kufic and Nagari characters.

NOTE

• Other UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Delhi: Humayun's Tomb (1993) and the Red Fort Complex (2007).

• Agra has the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri; Chandigarh has Le Corbusier's Capitol Complex.

question: Which is the most obvious symptom of infantile jaundice that usually appears between the second and fourth day after birth?
option_1: Cracking and irritation at the corners of mouth
option_3: Yellowing of the skin and the whites of the eyes
option_4: Swelling and bleeding of the gums
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yellowing of the skin and the whites of the eyes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Infantile (neonatal) jaundice most obviously shows itself as a yellow discolouration of the skin and of the sclera (the whites of the eyes), usually appearing between the second and fourth day after birth. (नवजात पीलिया — त्वचा और आँखों का पीला पड़ना)

• It is caused by a high level of "bilirubin" in the blood (hyperbilirubinaemia). A newborn's immature liver cannot process bilirubin — the yellow pigment released when red blood cells break down — fast enough.

• The yellowing typically starts on the face and spreads downwards to the chest, abdomen and limbs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Mild physiological jaundice usually clears in 1–2 weeks without treatment. Severe cases are treated with phototherapy (blue light converts bilirubin into a form easily excreted) or, rarely, exchange transfusion.

• If left untreated, very high bilirubin can cause brain damage known as "kernicterus".

NOTE

• Other options relate to different deficiencies: cracking at the corners of the mouth (angular stomatitis) — Vitamin B2 (riboflavin) deficiency; swollen/puffy ankles (oedema) — protein deficiency/kidney or heart problems; swelling and bleeding gums (scurvy) — Vitamin C deficiency.

question: The Units of Linear momentum are measured in _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is kg m/s.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Linear momentum (p) is defined as the product of an object's mass (m) and its velocity (v):

◦ p = m × v

• Therefore its SI unit = unit of mass × unit of velocity = kilogram × metre per second = kg m/s (also written as kg m s⁻¹, and equivalently newton-second, N s). (रैखिक संवेग — kg m/s)

• Momentum is a vector quantity; its direction is the same as that of the velocity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "kg m/s²" is the unit of force (newton), since F = ma.

• Options 1 and 3 ("kg² m/s", "k²g m/s") are meaningless — mass is never squared in momentum.

• Newton's Second Law states that force is the rate of change of momentum: F = dp/dt = ma.

• Impulse = Force × time = change in momentum, and also has the unit N s = kg m/s.

NOTE

• Law of Conservation of Linear Momentum: in the absence of an external force, the total momentum of a system remains constant. It explains recoil of a gun, rocket propulsion and collisions.

• Related SI units: Work/Energy — joule (J = kg m²/s²), Power — watt (W = J/s), Pressure — pascal (Pa = N/m²).

question: In which of the following cities the 2023 SAFF Championship was held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bengaluru.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 2023 SAFF Championship (the 14th edition) was held in Bengaluru, Karnataka, at the Sree Kanteerava Stadium, from 21 June to 4 July 2023. (सैफ चैंपियनशिप 2023 — बेंगलुरु)

• India won the title, defeating Kuwait in the final by 5–4 in the penalty shoot-out after the match ended 1–1. It was India's 9th SAFF Championship title.

• India's captain Sunil Chhetri was the top scorer of the tournament.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• SAFF stands for the South Asian Football Federation, founded in 1997, with headquarters in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Its members include India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives, Sri Lanka and Pakistan.

• Kuwait and Lebanon were invited as guest teams in the 2023 edition.

NOTE

• India is by far the most successful team in the SAFF Championship. The All India Football Federation (AIFF) was founded in 1937; world football is governed by FIFA (founded 1904, headquarters Zurich, Switzerland).

• The Sree Kanteerava Stadium in Bengaluru is also the home ground of Bengaluru FC.

question: Mirabai Chanu was selected as BBC Indian Sportswoman of the Year 2022. She is related to which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Weightlifting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Saikhom Mirabai Chanu, from Manipur, is an Indian weightlifter who competes in the 49 kg category. She was named the BBC Indian Sportswoman of the Year 2022. (भारोत्तोलन — मीराबाई चानू)

• She won the silver medal at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021) — India's first medal of those Games and only the second-ever Olympic weightlifting medal for India after Karnam Malleswari (Sydney 2000).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Mirabai Chanu also won gold at the 2017 World Weightlifting Championships (Anaheim) and gold at the Commonwealth Games 2018 (Gold Coast) and 2022 (Birmingham).

• She has been honoured with the Padma Shri (2018) and the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna / Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (2018).

• In weightlifting, two lifts are performed: the snatch and the clean & jerk; the total decides the winner.

NOTE

• BBC Indian Sportswoman of the Year winners: Dutee Chand (2019), P. V. Sindhu (2020), Mirabai Chanu (2021 and 2022).

• Famous Indians in the other listed sports: Neeraj Chopra (javelin), Krishna Poonia/Seema Punia (discus), Mary Kom/Nikhat Zareen (boxing).

question: Punjab state is rich in which natural resource from the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fertile soil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Punjab is essentially an alluvial plain formed by the rivers of the Indus system, and its greatest natural resource is its highly fertile alluvial soil, supported by extensive canal irrigation and groundwater. (उपजाऊ मिट्टी)

• Because of this, Punjab is called the "Granary of India" or the "Bread Basket of India" and was the heartland of the Green Revolution of the 1960s. It contributes a very large share of wheat and rice to the central pool.

• The name "Punjab" means "the land of five rivers" — Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab and Jhelum (the first three flow through present-day Indian Punjab).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Punjab has no significant mineral wealth — it lacks coal, petroleum and metallic ores.

• Coal in India is found mainly in Jharkhand (Jharia, Bokaro), Odisha, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal (Raniganj) and Madhya Pradesh.

• Petroleum is produced mainly from Mumbai High, Gujarat (Ankleshwar) and Assam (Digboi, Naharkatiya).

NOTE

• The Green Revolution in India was led by Dr M. S. Swaminathan (with Norman Borlaug) and was most successful in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.

• Alluvial soil is the most widespread soil in India, rich in potash and lime but deficient in nitrogen and phosphorus.

question: How many schedules are there in our Constitution as of June 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 12.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of June 2023, the Constitution of India has 12 Schedules. (भारतीय संविधान में 12 अनुसूचियाँ)

• The original Constitution (1950) had only 8 Schedules; four more were added later by amendments:

◦ 9th Schedule — added by the 1st Amendment Act, 1951 (laws protected from judicial review, mainly land reform laws).

◦ 10th Schedule — added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 (Anti-Defection Law).

◦ 11th Schedule — added by the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 (Panchayati Raj — 29 subjects).

◦ 12th Schedule — added by the 74th Amendment Act, 1992 (Municipalities — 18 subjects).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• 1st Schedule — States and Union Territories; 2nd — emoluments of high officials; 3rd — forms of oaths/affirmations; 4th — allocation of Rajya Sabha seats; 5th — administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes; 6th — tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram; 7th — Union, State and Concurrent Lists; 8th — official languages (22 languages).

NOTE

• The Constitution presently has about 470 Articles in 25 Parts and 12 Schedules; it was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

• Dr B. R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee; the Constituent Assembly's first meeting was on 9 December 1946.
